newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT-Bompreco still a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Bompreco still a buy.

text.p: Robert Fleming & Co Ltd said it has reiterated its buy recommendation on Brazilian food retailer Bompreco, which just bought Bahia state supermarket chain Supermar for 65 million reais ($60 million).
-- "With Supermar, Bompreco is now the third-largest food retailer in Latin America," Flemings analyst Thomas Mobille wrote in a report.
-- Bompreco trades at a 24-percent discount to Brazilian supermarket chain Pao de Acucar and is one of Latin America's most attractive food retail stocks, he added.
-- The most dramatic improvements in Bompreco's efficiency and bottom line should come in 1999 and 2000, so "we recommend accumulating the stock," he said.

-- Bompreco has excellent growth prospects compared with other food retailers in Latin America and Supermar's Bahia state market compliments its core market of Recife in nearby Pernambuco state, he added.
-- Because the purchase of Supermar included assumption of 218 million reais in Supermar's debt, the purchase price was actually 283 million reais, Mobille said.

-- But the chain's operations compliment Bompreco's existing operations, instantly increasing its floor space, selling area and net sales by 106 percent, 80 percent and 59 percent respectively, he added.
-- Bompreco's preferred closed June 13 at 13.04 reais.
